# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Kripke HPC benchmark on an AWS ARM-based CPU instance within a Kubernetes cluster.
# It is configured for a single-node execution, utilizing AWS EFA for high-performance networking.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using a unique name to prevent collisions with previous experiments.
  name: kripke-aws-cpu-run-4
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The size corresponds to the number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to satisfy the requirement to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to launch for the job.
  # These tasks will be distributed across the pods (in this case, all on one pod).
  tasks: 4

  # Pods will not be deleted after the job completes, allowing for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enforce strict schema validation for the MiniCluster spec.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture is ARM, which is required for ARM-based instances.
    arch: "arm"
    # Override the default Flux container to use an ARM-compatible image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to execute. The Flux operator automatically wraps this with 'flux run'.
      command: kripke
      # This container is a worker, not the launcher pod that submits the job.
      launcher: false
      # Resource requests and limits for the pod.
      # This requests an AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for high-speed, low-latency networking.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest addresses the previous run's application-level failure.
# It is configured to run the Kripke HPC benchmark on a single AWS ARM-based CPU instance with EFA networking.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using a new, unique name to avoid collisions and track this corrected attempt.
  name: kripke-aws-cpu-run-5
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 for single-node execution.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to launch for the job.
  tasks: 4

  # Pods will not be deleted after the job completes, allowing for post-run inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enforce strict schema validation for the MiniCluster spec.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific configuration tailored for the ARM/EFA environment.
  flux:
    # Fix: Add required option flag for cpu affinity to ensure proper task placement.
    optionFlags: "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"
    # Specify the architecture is ARM, as required for the instance type.
    arch: "arm"
    # Override the default Flux container to use an ARM-compatible image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # This container is a worker, not the launcher pod.
      launcher: false

      # Fix: The command is updated to tell Kripke how to decompose the problem across the 4 MPI tasks, resolving the assertion failure.
      command: kripke --procs 2,2,1

      # Fix: Add required environment variables to configure libfabric for AWS EFA.
      environment:
        FI_PROVIDER: efa
        FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA: "1"

      # Resource requests and limits for the pod.
      # This requests an AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for high-speed, low-latency networking.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
